text: Restless, shifting, fugitive as time itself is a certain vast bulk of the population of the red brick district of the lower West Side. <break time="0.8s" /> They are homeless, yet they have a hundred homes, and they drift from furnished room to furnished room, transients forever, in their lodging as in their hearts and minds. <break time="0.8s" /> Such houses must hold a thousand tales, most of them dull, but it would be strange if no ghost could be found among so many guests. <break time="0.8s" /> One evening after dark, a young man wandered among these crumbling red mansions, ringing their bells, and at the twelfth house he rested his small handbag upon the step. <break time="0.8s" /> He wiped the dust from his hatband and forehead, and the bell sounded faint and far away in some remote, hollow depth of the house. <break time="0.8s" /> To the door came a housekeeper who reminded him of an unwholesome, overfed worm, and he asked her in a low voice whether there was a room to let. <break time="0.8s" /> Come in, said the housekeeper, whose voice seemed to come from a throat lined with fur, I have the third floor back, which has been vacant for a week. <break time="0.8s" /> He followed her up the stairs, where a faint light softened the shadows, and the carpet under his feet had decayed until it looked like moss growing on stone.
